subject: URGENT: 5xx spike + node evictions during morning peak — customer impact
messages:
From: Naomi Brooks <naomi@edgewave.io>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: sre@edgewave.io
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 08:12:34 -0800
Subject: 5xx spike this AM — production requests failing

Hi Priyom,

We had a pretty bad morning window (07:45–08:20 PT) where ~18% of requests to our inference endpoint returned 5xx or timed out. User-facing errors spiked and our retries amplified the traffic. We captured a sample of logs and a couple of request IDs — attaching a trimmed log snippet.

Observations from our side:
- Latency jumped from ~120ms to 900–1,200ms before errors.
- Multiple backend nodes were evicted (kicked) around 07:50 PT per our kube-controller view.
- Retries from our client (~3x per request) coincided with elevated 429/503 counts.

This is impacting our enterprise customers. We need a quick root cause and mitigation; please escalate to your on-call or exec if needed.

Request IDs: rID-6a3f, rID-6a7b
Attached: edgewave-5xx-sample-logs-20261218.txt

Thanks,
Naomi Brooks
Head of Platform Reliability
EdgeWave

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Naomi Brooks <naomi@edgewave.io>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 08:28:12 -08:00
Subject: Re: 5xx spike this AM — production requests failing

Naomi — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. I’m escalating this immediately. Initial read: sounds like a combination of backend node evictions in the Dedicated pool and autoscale lag which allowed queue depth to blow up and surface 5xx.

Immediate actions we are taking:
- Sean is triaging the Dedicated pool telemetry and eviction traces.
- Monica is pulling kernel/gpu driver events and quantization memory stats for the affected nodes.
- I’m creating a priority incident (SUP-5821) and will request a short maintenance window to force a controlled drain & restart if needed.

Could you confirm whether EdgeWave was running pinned model version v2026-11-15 or the canary v2026-12-01? That will help rule out a model change.

I’ll follow up within 30 minutes with an initial ETA.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Naomi Brooks <naomi@edgewave.io>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 08:43:01 -08:00
Subject: Re: 5xx spike this AM — production requests failing

Adding notes from initial triage (timeline + telemetry):

- 07:38 PT: workload begins to ramp (customer traffic pattern).
- 07:46 PT: autoscaler saw a sudden queue depth spike and issued scale-up but internal backoff delayed launch of new nodes by ~35s due to image pull + GPU driver warmup on Dedicated fleet.
- 07:50 PT: controller evicted three nodes with OOM-like driver resets (nv-host-reset events). That produced transient 503s while remaining nodes absorbed extra KV cache pressure.
- 07:54 PT: retry amplification from clients increased QPS to 2.6x steady state for ~6 minutes.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Temporarily increased connection queue window and raised per-tenant tokenized rate limit to reduce retry amplification.
- Triggered emergency pool scale (cold node preboot triggered) and pre-warmed two GPUs from a warm image snapshot to shorten init time.

Next steps (requested by me):
1) Engineering to validate image snapshot health and driver compatibility.
2) Ops to add a short-lived autoscale policy override for EdgeWave Dedicated pool (keep extra buffer nodes for 24h).
3) Product to notify customer success and offer credits for the incident if SLA hit.

I’m handing to Monica for logs and kernel-level detail. Laura — can you prepare an exec note if this needs leadership visibility?

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Incident Response Lead, Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Naomi Brooks <naomi@edgewave.io>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:22:53 -08:00
Subject: Re: 5xx spike this AM — production requests failing

Attached snapshot and a brief correlate of kernel/gpu driver events with our eviction logs. Key findings:
- Three nodes reported NV-HOST-RESET around 07:49:32. Exact kernel message: "nv-host-reset: GPU reset due to MMU fault".
- Memory allocations for KV cache spiked 2.8x on surviving nodes during the retry window; cache thrashing observed.
- Autoscaler cold-start time median: 43s (image pull + driver init). Warm-snapshot median: 9s.

Suggested immediate action:
- Short-term: pin EdgeWave pool to use warm-image snapshot for 48h and set min-replicas = current+2 to blunt eviction risk. Ops can revert after stabilization.
- Mid-term: create a pre-warm lifecycle for Dedicated pools that maintains 1 warm standby per 20 active GPUs.

I’ve uploaded the full logs to the Drive link and attached the autoscale-timeline PNG.

Attachments: autoscale-timeline-20261218.png

— Monica Patel
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Naomi Brooks <naomi@edgewave.io>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 11:42:10 -08:00
Subject: Re: 5xx spike this AM — production requests failing

Hi Naomi — quick update and proposed closure:

Summary of what happened: autoscale lag + cold-start driver resets led to node evictions; retries amplified QPS and caused temporary KV cache pressure on surviving nodes which surfaced 503/504 errors for ~6 minutes.

What we did:
- Pre-warmed two GPUs using warm snapshot and increased min-replicas for EdgeWave Dedicated pool for 24 hours.
- Tuned per-tenant rate window and enabled short-term retry dampening for EdgeWave client tokens.
- Ops has scheduled the warm-standby policy change into the runway; engineering will run a driver compatibility smoke test this week.

Impact: customer-visible errors lasted ~6 minutes; latency degraded during that window. We do not currently see persistent SLA violations beyond the incident window.

Next steps / asks for EdgeWave:
- Can your SRE confirm whether client SDK retried by default (3x)? If so, we recommend switching to exponential backoff jitter for SDK v2.
- Accept the warm-image temporary policy for 24h so we can monitor and then revert.

If you’d like, Laura will prepare a short exec summary for your leadership and ours. We can also open a joint post-incident review (PIE) with logs and timing.

Thanks for your patience — we’ll follow up with the PIE draft next week.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
